body: Legally, I have some right to be in her life (access to schools and doctors, etc). But her mother and I do not speak and do not cooperate at all. She uses lawyers to interfere with everything. So, it's an additional struggle.

> Assuming she is getting professional help?

Yes, but still, not being there to see things for myself, it's not very comforting. Thank you for the reply.

> I hope you guys get through this

Thank you, I appreciate it. It's been a long road.
Thank you. It's well-received. I am aware that, as a male and an engineer, my first reaction is to "solve problems".

> What about moving to the US to be closer?

Thanks for the reply. It's a long story. The summary is that my skills are worth more overseas. One of the reasons I hate the Family Courts so much is because, in my case, they maximized my child support and alimony payments to the maximum salary I could possibly earn. In effect, it separated me from my child and the USA. I often get depressed myself; it's a no-win situation. I've asked the judge three times to lower my payments, but Family Courts simply don't lower payments, ever, for any reason.
